title: Evaluating Quality and Engagement of Medical Information on LASIK, LASEK, and SMILE in TikTok Videos
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of 240 English-language TikTok videos on laser refractive surgery, January 2025. The study is overwhelmingly a DISCERN quality study, which on its own would be QUALITY-ONLY and excluded - but it also carries one explicit falsity variable: the coders recorded 'subjectively harmful misinformation as determined by the grader' for each video, and report that 1 of 240 (0.4%) contained potentially harmful misinformation. That is a share of items in a sample explicitly coded as misinformation, with a denominator, so the paper is INCLUDE with one CONTENT row. The DISCERN result (64.6% poor or very poor) is recorded alongside as a construct=QUALITY row, kept for the appendix and excluded from prevalence per section 3.

estimates.country: Not stated (English-language TikTok content; authors are US-based)
estimates.date: January 2025 (all videos retrieved on the same day; non-time-dependent variables coded over the following 2 weeks)
estimates.measure_type: % of laser-refractive-surgery TikTok videos containing potentially harmful misinformation
estimates.value_raw: One video (0.4%) contained potentially harmful misinformation [1/240]
estimates.denominator: 240 English-language TikTok videos on LASIK (180), LASEK (30) and SMILE (30), collected in January 2025 from a fixed quota of videos per LRS hashtag (#lasik 30, #lasikeyesurgery 30, #lasikeyesurgerycheck 30, #lasiksurgery 25, #lasikcomplication 25, #lasikjourney 20, #lasikdoctor 20, #lasek 30, #smileeyesurgery 30), each with over 1000 views
estimates.definition: A grader flagged the video as containing 'subjectively harmful misinformation'; the single flagged video was a patient's step-by-step personal account of LASIK whose 'language was not fully medically accurate and could provoke unnecessary fears in potential patients'
estimates.misinfo_def: "subjectively harmful misinformation as determined by the grader" - no external ground truth, guideline or fact-check is named
estimates.source_quote: One video (0.4%) contained potentially harmful misinformation.
estimates.page_loc: Results 3.1 Video Characteristics, p. 4; Abstract Results ("0.4% contained potentially harmful misinformation"); described in the Discussion ("Misinformation was rarely overt; only one video was flagged as potentially harmful.")
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two independent, NON-BLINDED reviewers (University of Miami / Bascom Palmer ophthalmology authors) graded each video on a standardised coding form, then compared results and discussed discrepancies to consensus, producing a single agreed dataset. No kappa or other agreement statistic is reported ('interrater consistency was ensured through standardised reviewer training and reconciliation of scoring discrepancies'). The misinformation variable is explicitly labelled subjective and grader-determined.
estimates.moderator_quote: Additional indicators included the presence of medical recommendations, discussion of risks or alternatives, reference to quality-of-life effects, overtly favorable or unfavorable stance toward LRS, and subjectively harmful misinformation as determined by the grader.
estimates.notes: ADJUDICATOR: n = 1. The estimate is a single flagged video, so its confidence interval is enormous and it should not carry weight in any pooled analysis. The threshold is also idiosyncratic - 'potentially HARMFUL' misinformation, subjectively determined, not simply false content - so this measures overt danger, not falsity, and is not comparable to studies coding any inaccuracy. The authors themselves say the real problem was omission, not overt falsehood ('Misinformation was rarely overt ... However, omission bias was pervasive. Seventy-two percent of videos were anecdotal and frequently lacked discussion of complications or eligibility criteria. Even factually accurate content may mislead when critical context is absent.'), which is exactly the situation section 3 assigns to QUALITY rather than CONTENT. Coded CONTENT only because the variable is an explicit misinformation flag with a stated denominator. Denominator is hashtag-quota-sampled and >1000-view-filtered, hence denom_selection=curated; the sample is not representative of LRS content on TikTok. Country is Global because the only stated restriction is English language.

estimates.country: Not stated (English-language TikTok content; authors are US-based)
estimates.measure_type: % of laser-refractive-surgery TikTok videos rated poor or very poor in overall educational quality on the DISCERN instrument
estimates.value_raw: 64.6% were rated poor or very poor in overall quality [119 (49.6%) poor + 36 (15.0%) very poor of 240]
estimates.denominator: The same 240 English-language TikTok LRS videos
estimates.definition: Total DISCERN score (15 items, each 1-5, range 15-75) falling in the poor (27-38) or very poor (15-26) band
estimates.misinfo_def: n/a - DISCERN rates the reliability and completeness of consumer health information (clear aims, sources, balance, discussion of risks, alternatives, shared decision-making), not the truth of the claims made
estimates.source_quote: Of 240 videos analyzed, 64.6% were rated poor or very poor in overall quality, and 0.4% contained potentially harmful misinformation.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results; component counts in Results 3.1 ("Nine videos achieved an overall quality DISCERN score of good (3.8%), 76 (31.7%) fair, 119 (49.6%) poor, and 36 (15.0%) very poor.")
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same two non-blinded reviewers, consensus-reconciled; DISCERN is a validated 15-item instrument for consumer health information, applied here to video (the authors list its use on video as a limitation, since it was designed for written material). No interrater reliability statistic reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: The DISCERN instrument, a validated 15-question tool for assessing consumer health information quality, was used to assess information reliability and quality, where each item is scored from 1 to 5. Total DISCERN scores ranged from 15 to 75 and were categorized as excellent (63–75), good (51–62), fair (39–50), poor (27–38), or very poor (15–26).
estimates.notes: QUALITY row, kept for the appendix and EXCLUDED FROM PREVALENCE per section 3: a wholly accurate video can score 'very poor' on DISCERN for lacking sources or balance, so this is not a falsity measure. The 64.6% is stated verbatim in the Abstract, so R8 is satisfied without my summing the two component bands (which do reconcile: 49.6 + 15.0 = 64.6, i.e. 155/240). Minor internal inconsistency worth noting: the Results paragraph calls these bands the 'overall quality DISCERN score' while the mean 'overall DISCERN rating' of 2.9 (SD 1.0) is the separate 16th item on a 1-5 scale, which the Methods say was recorded but excluded from the total.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) 'Most (86.7%) were subjectively rated satisfactory' - the reviewers' own satisfactory/poor gestalt rating; the complement (13.3% poor) would be a second QUALITY row, but it is a redundant subjective duplicate of the DISCERN banding and the complement is not stated verbatim, so no row (R8). (2) Content-composition shares that are NOT falsity measures and so generate no rows: anecdotal 72.5% / educational 21.3% / commercial 6.3%; medical recommendations present 30.8%; favorable portrayal of surgery 82.9%; symptoms discussed 22.5% (ocular pain 7.5%); independent creators 60.0%; physicians 39.6%; MD degree disclosed 23.3%; educational videos rated satisfactory 94.1% vs 46.7% for commercial. (3) 'Seventy-two percent of videos were anecdotal and frequently lacked discussion of complications or eligibility criteria' - an omission-bias statement, and the authors explicitly say 'Even factually accurate content may mislead when critical context is absent', which is the section-3 definition of QUALITY, not CONTENT; no row. (4) All DISCERN domain means (additional sources 1.04, source time 1.05, balance and unbiased 1.37, sources 1.75, treatment risks 1.73 ...), the t-test and ANOVA comparisons (LASEK vs LASIK, physician vs non-physician, independent vs for-profit) and the regression coefficients are scale means or model estimates, not shares - no rows per the 'scale MEANS only' rule. (5) Figures the paper cites from elsewhere are excluded per R8: 31% of oculoplastic Reddit statements medically inaccurate [14]; Haddad and Saade's mean DISCERN 1.67/5 and 26% ophthalmologist-produced [15]; Fazio et al.'s 39.6% healthcare-professional-produced [16]. (6) No exposure, reach, sharing or concentration statistic is reported: view/like/share counts are given only as means with SDs (mean views 647,793.1, SD 2,711,392.1), never as a share of exposure attributable to misinformation, so R1 cannot be met and no CONCENTRATION row is possible - though the huge SDs do show the view distribution is extremely skewed.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis of 240 English-language TikTok videos on LASIK (180), LASEK (30) and SMILE (30), January 2025. Sampling: a newly created TikTok account (to limit algorithmic personalisation) searched nine LRS hashtags chosen after informal browsing on a separate account, with a fixed quota per hashtag; inclusion required public accessibility, English, >1000 views and a clear focus on LASIK/LASEK/SMILE; duplicates, off-topic and purely promotional videos were excluded. PRK hashtags were deliberately omitted. All videos retrieved the same day with engagement metrics captured at collection; other variables coded over 2 weeks. Coding: two independent, NON-BLINDED reviewers on a standardised form, discrepancies reconciled to consensus into a single dataset; interrater agreement asserted through training and reconciliation but NO kappa or ICC is reported. Instruments: 15-item DISCERN (total 15-75, banded excellent/good/fair/poor/very poor) plus bespoke content indicators including a subjective 'harmful misinformation' flag and a subjective satisfactory/poor rating. Engagement = (likes + comments + shares) / views x 100. Analysis in Excel and R 4.3.1; t tests, chi-square, linear regression, ANOVA with Tukey HSD; alpha = 0.05, two-sided. IRB-exempt. Author-stated limitations: DISCERN was designed for written material, single-timepoint sampling, English-only. Additional risks for this review: quota-by-hashtag sampling with a >1000-view floor (not representative), non-blinded coders, no reliability statistic, and a misinformation variable that is explicitly subjective and yields a single positive case.
